questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A completely new culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, it has been a truly amazing exchange stay. I have met so many beautiful people from many different countries and cultures and I have got some really great friends. The only reason, why I don't give my overall stay a 10, is the fact that the university is located 35-45 minutes away with public transport (direct train) from the city center of Barcelona and the university sometimes was a little bit confusing. But those downsides are small things in the bigger picture.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first day of school, there was an information event for all the new exchange students at the faculty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Vila Universitària UAB.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different meal possibilities at the university. In the student housing area (Vila), there are two cafes where you can eat and a little supermarket. All the student apartments are equipped with kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Keep in mind that the university and the campus are located 35-45 minutes away from Barcelona city center with public transport (direct train). The good thing is that public transport is very cheap compared to Copenhagen and Denmark. The rent price at campus is also lower compared to the city center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The student apartments at campus are not the newest ones anymore. But they are still quite good.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Manuals in pdf format sent by the university administration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do it before deadline.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All courses are 6 ECTS points.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is dependent on which courses you take. But generally, the level is quite high. Generally, I will say that the level is the same as UCPH, maybe a bit less. But this is dependent on which courses you take as mentioned before. The exam level and the difficulty of this are generally lower compared to the exam level at UCPH, I will say.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's more gymnasium/high school style at UAB. In some courses for example, there are attendance requirements. Assignments during the semester will also often be a part of your final grade at UAB.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Public Finance (6 ECTS)
- Public Sector Economics (6 ECTS)
- Finance II (6 ECTS)
- Strategic Management II (6 ECTS)
- Operations Management (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Finance II

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Nothing.
*Communication: Streaming services included in the cost.
*Housing: Single apartment (with your own kitchen and bathroom) in the Vila (student housing at campus)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Less expensive than expected: Public Transport
More expensive than expected: Groceries, restaurants, cafes
The difference in the cost of living compared to Copenhagen and Denmark is not so big as expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't know because I didn't use it. In the Vila (campus/student housing), there was a football pitch where we played football weekly.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN makes a lot of activities but I didn't really use it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the other parts of Spain. Especially the Basque Country, I will recommend (especially San Sebastian).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, there can often be a language barrier if you don't speak Spanish (and sometimes Catalan).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- It can be good to know at least a little bit of Spanish (or Catalan) before coming
- Be active in socializing in the beginning so you can get some friends
- Explore Barcelona

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I have met so many beautiful people from many different countries and cultures and I have got friends for life.
It was a great experience to watch FC Barcelona and be in Camp Nou so often (look out for "6 matches packages"). It was also a great experience to watch Espanyol (great atmosphere). So, if you are a football fan, also remember to look out for Espanyol.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning where you don't know anybody.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
